character_facts: Steelhead is associated with an internal split involving the poet Zaran Klezra and is described here as capable of extreme ruthlessness.
Dona Vicenta comes to hate Steelhead, contracts tuberculosis, and carries twins with different fathers according to the recap.
Zaran Klezra is identified as the father of the female twin.
Tonto is the one recounting these prior events on this page.
Lothar is specifically said to wonder how the Metabaron succession tradition can be preserved after Steelhead's choice.

lore_facts: The Metabarons' line is said to pass only from father to son.
Philodendra contains valuable bikramen, important enough to attract galaxy-wide military and economic attention.
The Techno-Technos are an opposing power with a stronghold and a ruling TechnoPope.
The Troglosocialists are a population whose relocation can be negotiated as part of planetary sale.
A new artificial world exists and becomes the relocation site after the sale of Philodendra.
plot_events: The page recounts Don Nicanor's death and says Steelhead, after removing the part of himself associated with the poet Zaran Klezra, joins the war against the Techno-Technos.
During the battle, Dona Vicenta realizes how cold and ruthless Steelhead truly is and begins to hate him.
Although Steelhead wins, Philodendra is described as almost entirely destroyed.
Steelhead launches a plan to infiltrate the Techno-Techno stronghold, abduct the reigning TechnoPope, and bring him back to Philodendra.
A vast siege forms around the planet, and Steelhead publicizes the value of bikramen there, drawing major outside interest and fleets from across the galaxy.
With Dona Vicenta's reluctant help, Steelhead negotiates the sale of the planet and the relocation of the Troglosocialists to another world.
On the new artificial world, Dona Vicenta develops tuberculosis and later reveals she is pregnant with twins: a boy by Steelhead and a girl by Zaran.
Tonto says complications allow only one baby to be born, and Dona Vicenta assumes Steelhead will choose the male heir.
The recap ends by stating that Steelhead instead chooses the female child, raising doubt about how the Metabarons' father-to-son succession can continue.
